sentences.text: Location: High ...RESPONDENT Court of Karnataka (BY SRI VIRANAGOUDA MALIPATIL, HCGP)

THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 54(1) OF THE LAND  ACQUISITION ACT PRAYING TO, ALLOW THIS APPEAL WITH  COSTS AND MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD PASSED BY  THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, RAICHUR (SITTING AT ITINERATE  COURT, DEVADURGA) DATED 27.02.2015 IN LAC NO.229/2012  AND FIX THE MARKET VALUE FOR LAND ACQUIRED AT THE  -2-  MFA No. 200938 of 2015 Hussainsab S/O Khajasab vs The Spl Land Acquisition Officer on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44604907/
1 RATE OF RS.3,60,000/- PER ACRE AND AWARD ALL STATUTORY BENEFITS.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The appellant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation determined by the Additional Senior Civil Judge, Raichur in LAC No.229/2012, vide judgment and award dated 27.02.2015.
2.

The appellant claimed to be the owner of the land bearing Sy.No.39/A/1 (39/2) of Devaragudda village measuring 1 acre 30 guntas, which was proposed for acquisition for the purpose of N.R.B.C.
right bank canal project at Devaragudda village of Devadurga Taluk under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act on 28.11.2010.

The Land Acquisition Officer inspected the land and found that there was a well in an area measuring 0.47 guntas and determined the compensation payable at a sum of Rs.40,000/- per acre in respect of dry land and a sum of Rs.31,056/- towards well and passed award determining the total compensation payable to the appellant at a sum of Rs.1,01,521/-.
The compensation payable towards three tamarind trees was to be determined after obtaining the valuation from the concerned department.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant sought reference before the Reference Court.

The Reference Court after considering oral and documentary evidence, held that the spot inspection of the Land Acquisition Officer disclosed the existence of a well and therefore, enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.1,95,000/- per acre.
However, insofar as well is concerned, the Reference Court did not determine the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation enhanced by the Reference Court and the non-payment of compensation for the well and the tamarind trees, the present appeal is filed.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the existence of the well in the land in question is not in dispute.
He submits that the revenue records disclosed that the appellant was raising cotton and sunflower in the acquired land.
He submits that when the land was dry and not irrigated, the appellant could not have raised two crops in the year.

He therefore, submits that the Land Acquisition Officer as well as the Reference Court must have considered the land in question as an irrigated land and it must have awarded compensation by taking the cotton and sunflower as the crops raised in the land in question.
He submits that the compensation awarded towards the well is also meager and requires enhancement.

He further submits that the appellant has obtained electricity for the purpose of lifting water from the land in question for the purpose of irrigation and therefore, the Land Acquisition Officer as well as the Reference Court must have considered this crucial aspect of the matter.
He further submits that the compensation payable in respect of three tamarind trees also needs to be determined.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent submits that the compensation of Rs.1,95,000/-
determined by the Reference Court was based on the judgment passed by this Court in Miscellaneous Second Appeal No.1131/2013 and other connected appeals and therefore, the compensation awarded by the Reference Court is just and proper and does not call for any Hussainsab S/O Khajasab vs The Spl Land Acquisition Officer on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44604907/
2 enhancement.
5. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned counsel for the respondent.
6. It is not in dispute that the appellant is the owner of the land in question namely Sy.No.39/A/1 (39/2) of Devaragudda village measuring 1 acre 30 guntas.
It is also not in dispute that a well exists in the land in question in an area measuring 0.47 gunta.
The revenue records for the year 2008-09 discloses that the appellant was raising cotton in the monsoon and sunflower in the dry season.
This is continued for the year 2009-10 and 2010-11.
The revenue records also discloses that a bore-well is sunk in the land in question.
Therefore, it can easily be held that the appellant was raising cotton and sunflower during the monsoon and dry season respectively.

Ex.P.6 is the yield certificate issued by the Agricultural University, Raichur, which shows that the yield of cotton per hectare is 20-25 quintals, while the yield of sunflower is 15-20 quintals per hectare.
The price list issued by the APMC, Raichur as per Ex.P.5 discloses that for the year 2010-11, the maximum price for hybrid cotton was Rs.6,650/- per quintal and Rs.3,419/- per quintal for sunflower.
Ex.P.7 shows that the appellant had got the installation serviced with electricity on 31.03.2011.
There is no contra evidence to establish that the appellant was not raising any crop in the land in question.

In that view of the matter, the Land Acquisition Officer as well as the Reference Court must have determined the compensation based on crop capitalization method by taking sunflower and cotton, as crops raised by the appellant in the land in question.
The Land Acquisition Officer as well as the Reference Court must have considered 50% of the yield as expenses and thereafter, must have determined the compensation.
Similarly, the Land Acquisition Officer as well as the Reference Court must have considered the value of the well sunk in the land in question by taking the rates as prevalent in the year 2010-11.
The value of the three tamarind trees also must have been assessed by taking the crop capitalization method and the crop value of each tree at a sum of Rs.15,000/-.

Since the Land Acquisition Officer as well as the Reference Court have failed to do so, but have determined the compensation based on the judgment of this Court in MSA No.1131/2013 and other connected appeals, which is applicable only in respect of dry land, which had no source of irrigation, the Reference Court committed an error in drawing a parallel between this case and the case in MSA No.1131/2013.
In that view of the matter, this appeal deserves to be allowed in part and is accordingly allowed in part.
The compensation payable to the appellant is re-
determined on the basis of crop capitalized method as follows:

Compensation payable in respect of 1 acre 30 guntas:
1. Cotton: 9 Quintals x Rs.6,650/- x 1/2 (expenses) x 10 (multiplier)= Rs.2,99,250/-
2. Sunflower: 7 Quintals x Rs.3,419/- x 1/2 x 10 = Rs.1,19,665/-
Total Per Acre: Rs.4,18,915/-
3. Compensation towards well: Rs.50,000 Hussainsab S/O Khajasab vs The Spl Land Acquisition Officer on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44604907/
3
4. Compensation towards 3 tamarind trees Rs.45,000/-
The appellant is entitled to all statutory benefits, interest and cost.
The deficit Court fee, if any, shall be paid within a period of eight weeks.

Sd/-
